name: overhead-from-the-top
prompt: Every gang member wears a knitted balaclava covering the whole head, with no eye, nose or mouth holes; a large white ring is stitched round the face, and a red triangle sits high over the wearer's left eye (on the right of the picture, at about 2 o'clock); gloves on both hands, collars and cuffs closed, no skin showing anywhere. Vertical night photograph taken from the very top edge of an enormous pile of stacked paper inside an empty warehouse, the lens aimed straight down its sheer white cliff face of compressed page edges, which runs away from us and narrows towards a wet concrete floor far below. Across the bottom third of the frame, closest to the lens, lies the uppermost sheet, sharp enough to see its fibres, printed in heavy black capitals: THE RULES. Down at the foot of the paper wall, tiny with distance and a little out of focus, five gang members in today's British streetwear (puffer jackets, hoodies, tracksuit bottoms, trainers) stand in a loose huddle with heads tipped right back, so their masks face the lens; each balaclava is its own deep shade (bottle green, navy, oxblood, charcoal, plum). Several of them hold small handheld torches pointed up at us, the hard white beams climbing the paper face and catching the stitched white rings and red triangles so they flare against the dark cloth. Apart from the torches, the only light is a weak orange streetlamp glow leaking through one grimy high window and lying in a slanted patch on the puddled floor, where the torch beams also reflect. Almost everything else is deep black; wide-angle lens, steep downward perspective with strong convergence, the floor pulled far away, fine film grain, no fog, no lens flare stars. The feeling is of looking down from a great height at people who look small and determined.
